reason: I'll start the living-bone goal by following stem-cell descendants into the bone lineage.
expectation: I expect bone-lineage cells to develop over time, though they may need further steps to build living bone.

alternatives.reason: Mineralizing the collagen framework also looks relevant, but I want to start with the cells.
The lined capsule is a separate goal I can approach afterward.

effect: The lineage produces osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes, so I can now add living cells to the bone framework.
reaction: The distinction between matrix-producing and embedded bone cells is useful.
reason: I'll combine the bone cells with the collagen framework to build toward living bone.
expectation: I expect a bone framework containing living cells; mineral and blood supply may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Mineralizing the framework also advances the bone goal, but I want to incorporate the cells first.

effect: The framework now highlights cells and collagen together; mineral and blood supply remain to be added.
reaction: The clarification that this is a change in emphasis, not cell development, is helpful.
reason: Adding mineral advances the living-bone goal.
expectation: I expect a mineralized bone framework with cells, but blood supply may still need a separate step.

alternatives.reason: The lined capsule also serves a goal, but I want to continue the bone construction first.

effect: The bone cutaway now includes mineral, collagen and cells; the blood supply remains separate.
reaction: The fine channels connecting the bone cells are an interesting detail.
reason: Adding blood vessels should complete the supplied-bone construction.
expectation: I expect the arm-bone cutaways to show a blood supply alongside their cells and mineralized matrix.

alternatives.reason: The capsule also needs its lining, but I want to finish the bone first.

effect: The bones now have a blood supply, and a new goal calls for connecting them into a supported, movable joint.
reaction: The cutaway usefully distinguishes the vessel from the channels connecting bone cells.
reason: I'll line the fibrous sleeve to work toward the joint capsule goal.
expectation: I expect a capsule with a synovial lining that contributes slippery fluid; it may still need to be fitted around the bones.

alternatives.reason: Cartilage also seems important for the joint, but I want to prepare the capsule first.

effect: The sleeve now has a synovial lining, completing the capsule goal; the bones still need to be connected into a joint.
reaction: The lining's contribution to joint fluid makes its purpose clear.
reason: I'll add cartilage to the bone ends before assembling the joint.
expectation: I expect cartilage-covered arm bone ends, with the capsule and ligaments still needed for a supported joint.

alternatives.reason: The capsule could be fitted first, but I want to prepare the bone surfaces.

effect: The bone ends now have smooth cartilage surfaces; the capsule remains to be added.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: I'll fit the capsule to the cartilage-covered bones; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a fluid-lined elbow joint, possibly still needing ligaments for support.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered bone ends, with fluid helping the surfaces glide; ligaments remain to support the joint.
reaction: The connection between the lining, fluid and gliding surfaces is clear.
reason: I'll add the ligaments for support; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect a supported, movable elbow joint with ligaments spanning its sides.

effect: The ligaments complete the supported, movable elbow: the plan shows bending while resisting sideways movement. All chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The contrast between permitted movement and restraint is a satisfying final detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Assembling the enclosed elbow connected the synovial lining and fluid to cartilage surfaces that glide, making the parts' relationship clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding cells and then mineral felt somewhat repetitive because the actions changed which parts of an existing mature-bone cutaway were highlighted rather than building new tissue.

surprise.text: The lineage plan distinguished matrix-producing osteoblasts from osteocytes embedded in bone, with processes extending through tiny channels.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although combining bone cells with the mature framework took some adjustment: it represented a change in the illustration's emphasis, not the cells moving into place.

continue.text: I would continue: connecting the joint's lining, cartilage and ligaments to their functions made the final construction worthwhile, despite some repetitive highlighting steps.
